original.reason: It asserts \(\overline{B(\mathbf0,\varepsilon)}=[0,\varepsilon]^\omega\) without ensuring \(0<\varepsilon\le1\). For \(\varepsilon>1\), this displayed set is not even a subset of \([0,1]^\omega\). One can repair this by shrinking the radius first.

judgment.reason: It has the same unaddressed radius issue: \(\varepsilon\) need not be at most \(1\), so the claimed closure \([0,\varepsilon]^\omega\) is not correct as written.
It does not restrict or shrink \(\varepsilon\) to at most \(1\), making its asserted ball closure incorrect when \(\varepsilon>1\).
The claim that the closure is \([0,\varepsilon]^\omega\) requires \(\varepsilon\le1\), which is not established.
Its claimed equality between the ball closure and \([0,\varepsilon]^\omega\) likewise fails unless the radius is first chosen to satisfy \(\varepsilon\le1\).
